extracted.intended_audience: U.S. government officials, diplomats, and legislators (Congress/members deciding ratification); also legal practitioners dealing with consular law
extracted.subtask_description: Text of the 1788 Convention between France and the United States defining the functions, privileges, immunities, and procedures relating to Consuls and Vice-Consuls, together with Jefferson's commentary and recommendations on consular appointments and related policy. Useful for understanding legal rules and operational standards governing consular offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisions for delivery of Exequaturs and immediate enjoyment of privileges (Article I)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Consuls and Vice-Consuls named shall present their commissions according to established forms; they shall be delivered, without any charges, the Exequatur necessary for the exercise of their functions; and on exhibiting the said Exequatur, local authorities shall cause them to enjoy immediately, and without difficulty, the pre-eminences, authority, and privileges reciprocally granted, without exacting any fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes administrative procedure for recognition of consular officers and forbids any charge/fee for issuance; requires immediate deference by governors, tribunals, and officers upon presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immunity of chancery and persons attached; taxation and subject-to-law limits (Article II)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consuls, Vice-Consuls, and persons attached (chancellors, secretaries) shall enjoy full immunity for their chancery and its papers; they shall be exempt from personal military or civic services, billets, militia, watch, guardianship, trusteeship, and from duties, taxes, impositions, and charges whatsoever, except on real and personal estate they own which shall be subject to the taxes imposed on other individuals; in other instances they shall be subject to the laws of the land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants consular chancery inviolability and broad personal immunities while clarifying that private property and commercial activity remain taxable and that consuls are otherwise subject to domestic law; explicitly disclaims asylum for houses despite requirement to display sovereign arms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agents in ports; limits on their powers and immunities (Article III)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consuls and Vice-Consuls may establish agents in ports where needed; such agents may be merchants (national or foreign) furnished with a commission, confined to rendering services to merchants, navigators, and vessels and notifying the nearest Consul; they do not participate in consular immunities or have power to exact duties or emoluments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits local representation but restricts agents from exercising immunities or charging fees; stresses they are functional auxiliaries for service and communication only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consular chancery functions: acts, notarial functions, custody of seals (Article IV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consuls and Vice-Consuls may establish a chancery where consular determinations, acts, testaments, obligations, contracts, and effects from shipwreck are deposited; they may appoint and swear persons to act in chancery, commit custody of the seal, seal commissions, sentences, and perform notarial and registry functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizes consulates to operate as repositories and perform notarial/registry tasks for nationals' legal acts abroad; provides institutional basis for consular recordkeeping and formal acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive right to receive declarations, testaments, and to authenticate copies (Article V)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consuls and Vice-Consuls have the exclusive right to receive declarations and acts by captains, masters, crews, passengers, and merchants of their nation (including testaments); copies authenticated under the seal of the consulate shall have the same legal faith in tribunals as originals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants evidentiary privilege to consular-authenticated documents and exclusive receipt authority; also provides consuls power over administration of estates of deceased nationals within consulate bounds (inventory, liquidation, sale) with procedures requiring assistance of merchants and safeguards for creditor claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and safeguards in consular administration of deceased nationals' estates (Article V, continued)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consuls shall inventory, liquidate, and sell personal estate of deceased nationals with assistance of two merchants (or others if unavailable), deposit effects in chancery, and not deliver proceeds until debts contracted in the country are paid; creditors without written claims must give sufficient surety resident in the country. Consuls must notify death publicly and retain effects four months before delivering remaining estate to lawful successors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets timeline (four months) and creditor protections including attachment rights and surety requirements; balances protection of creditors and rights of lawful representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consular handling of average/loss declarations and maritime claims (Article VI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consuls and Vice-Consuls shall receive declarations, protests, and reports of captains and masters regarding average losses sustained at sea and shall lodge acts made in other ports; when only nationals are interested, consuls shall appoint skilful persons to settle damages and average, but where foreigners are interested the tribunals of the country decide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes consular competence (domestic-national maritime averages) from territorial courts' jurisdiction (cases involving other nationals); provides for consular facilitation of maritime loss documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consular duties on shipwrecks and salvage; custody and delivery of saved effects (Article VII)
rubrics_metrics.description: On shipwrecks, the nearest Consul or Vice-Consul shall act to save ship, cargo, and effects, take inventory, and secure effects without interference by military/customs/police; if no consul present or territorial judge is nearer, the judge shall act but retire to the consul on arrival and deliver report; saved goods to be deposited in Custom-house or safe place and delivered on consul order without process, either duty-free for re-export or with duty abatement if damaged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives consuls primary role in rescue, salvage inventory, and disposition; requires cooperation with territorial authorities and provides for duty exemptions/reductions and procedures to expedite owners' recovery or sale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consular police jurisdiction over vessels and limitation to interior matters (Article VIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consuls and Vice-Consuls shall exercise police over all vessels of their nation, holding power and jurisdiction in civil matters arising on board, with entire inspection over vessel, crew, and substitutions; they may go on board when necessary, but such functions are confined to the vessel interior and shall not interfere with port police.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes broad consular oversight of national vessels' internal civil affairs while preserving territorial authority over port policing; delimits consular competence to onboard matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to arrest deserters and demand their delivery (Article IX)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consuls and Vice-Consuls may cause to be arrested crew members who deserted, to send them back; they shall demand such deserters in writing from competent authorities proving their status by ship registers or rolls and shall receive assistance for search, seizure, and arrest; deserters may be detained at consul expense until sent back, but if not sent within three months they must be set at liberty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a procedure for repossessing deserters including requirement of documentary proof, cooperation by territorial authorities, financial responsibility by consul for detention, and a three-month release limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal accountability to territorial judges (Article X)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respective subjects or citizens who commit any crime or breach of the peace shall be amenable to the judges of the country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms territorial criminal jurisdiction over nationals; consuls do not immunize nationals from prosecution for crimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for seizure of offenders on board and notification to consul (Article XI)
rubrics_metrics.description: If offenders who are part of a ship's crew withdraw to the vessel, they may be seized there by order of territorial judges, who shall notify the Consul or Vice-Consul; notification shall not delay execution; persons arrested shall not be set at liberty until the consul is notified and may be delivered to consul if he requires, to be put aboard a vessel and sent out of the country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balances rapid execution of territorial orders with consul's right to receive custody and effect repatriation; notification requirement preserves consul's interests without obstructing justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consular jurisdiction over disputes between nationals and summary resolution (Article XII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences and suits between subjects/citizens of the contracting powers, particularly disputes regarding wages and engagement terms of crews, and disputes among crew members or between captains, shall be determined by respective Consuls and Vice-Consuls either by reference to arbitrators or by summary judgment, and without costs; no territorial officer shall interfere; appeals from consular sentences lie to the tribunals of France or the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes consular competence for intra-national commercial/maritime disputes with summary procedures and appeal path to territorial tribunals, and forbids interference by local civil or military officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to commercial tribunals and reciprocal arrangements (Article XIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Merchants of the U.S. shall enjoy the benefit of particular tribunals and forms established for expediting commercial affairs within the dominions of France; Congress will provide equivalent advantages for French merchants in the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires reciprocal expedited commercial justice for merchants of each nation and anticipates domestic legislative measures to secure equivalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption from personal service for proven nationals/residents (Article XIV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjects of France and citizens of the U.S. who shall prove by legal evidence that they are of the said nations respectively shall enjoy exemption from all personal service in the place of their settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affords exemption from conscription/forced personal service to proven nationals residing in the other country; requires legal proof of nationality/residence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most-favored-nation clause for consular pre-eminences (Article XV)
rubrics_metrics.description: If any other nation acquires by convention a treatment more favorable regarding consular pre-eminences, powers, and privileges, Consuls and Vice-Consuls of the contracting parties shall participate therein according to the treaty of amity and commerce provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures consular benefits remain at least equal to those granted third parties under future treaties (a consular most-favored-nation provision).

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of force and exchange of ratifications (Article XVI)
rubrics_metrics.description: The convention shall be in full force during twelve years from the exchange of ratifications, which shall be exchanged within one year if possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets explicit temporal duration (12 years) and procedural expectation for ratification exchange; provides termination/renewal cadence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jefferson's recommended rule: consul must be native citizen; vice-consul temporary dormancy (Jefferson's commentary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Jefferson proposes a standing law that 'no person but a native citizen shall be capable of the office of consul,' restricting that rule to consul (not vice-consul); during the consul's presence the vice-consul's functions should be suspended, and the vice-consul may be the best subject in the port (citizen or alien).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy rationale: native citizens better know language, laws, customs, commerce, have acquaintances, and are more reliable in fidelity; vice-consuls serve as counselors and become active only when consul absent, avoiding repeated commissioning/revoking and preserving the consul office for superior native appointees when they arrive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jefferson's recommended proscription of post-Mansfield English decisions (letter to Mr. Cutting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Jefferson recommends that in America any English decision which has happened since the accession of Lord Mansfield to the bench should never be cited in courts, because many of Mansfield's decisions contain 'sly poison' despite some good ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a normative legal standard Jefferson urges for American courts regarding admissible foreign precedent: proscribe a class of English authority (post-Mansfield) from citation to avoid adopting pernicious doctrines.
